title: Energy shock forces central banks to test whether inflation stays "headline-only"
summary: Bank of Canada, the ECB and the U.S. all frame the same risk: easing in energy-driven headline inflation may not translate into core prices, wages and expectations — where headline means the total inflation measure, while core strips out volatile food and energy — so policy is still waiting on evidence of whether the impulse spreads.

claims.text: Independent CSIS Futures Lab analysis (July 2026) offers alternative to pure terror/morale-break interpretation: Russian missile/drone campaign is a "geography of coercion" combining denial (disrupting logistics nodes, energy, ports, rail, air-defense) and punishment (pressure on civilians/political leadership), with damage increasingly concentrated in frontline/southern industrial oblasts and major urban centers; scaling is driven by Shahed-type drone mass production (5,000-6,000/month in late 2025 vs ~250 in Oct 2022) to probe air defenses cheaply, force Ukraine to expend costly interceptors, force dispersion of defenses, and widen area requiring protection.

claims.text: Same CSIS analysis finds coercive effect is cumulative rather than decisive and has not broken Ukrainian political cohesion or forced rapid settlement, despite sharply rising damage-days (358 in 2023 to 1,553 in 2025) and winter escalation (+24% Shahed launches, +14% cruise, +8% ballistic in winter months); western oblasts are struck less often due to distance from launch areas and better layered air-defense shielding, suggesting air-defense attrition and range constraints shape targeting alongside intent to cause civilian hardship.

claims.text: International humanitarian law has no formal "dual-use" category: under AP I art.52 and DoD Law of War Manual �5.6, an object is either a military objective (effective contribution to military action + definite military advantage) or civilian object; energy infrastructure may be assessed as military objective case-by-case (e.g., powering military industry) but proportionality and feasible precautions still apply, and reverberating civilian harm must be counted.
